newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Hang Seng seen at 15,000 year-end.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Hang Seng seen at 15,000 year-end.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index could reach 15,000 points by the end of the year, although range-bound trading was likely over the next couple of months as property prices corrected.
In its Hong Kong market outlook dated April 8, Merrill Lynch said it expected residential property prices to correct by 10 to 15 percent over the next two to three months.

"With potentially two more (interest) rate hikes in the pipeline, we sense that foreign investors approaching the last investment lap before the July 1 sovereignty change have found the perfect excuse to sit tight," it added.
"Consequently, the next couple of months could be sticky for Hong Kong equities with the index largely range bound."
The blue chip Hang Seng Index (HSI) closed Friday morning's session up 93.56 points at 12,452.26.
"We think the HSI could still reach 15,000 by the end of the year, although admittedly the odds are longer than three months ago," Merrill Lynch said.
"China liquidity developments, a more vibrant economic landscape and positive earnings momentum should provide an extra layer of support," it added.
Merrill Lynch said it expected reported earnings per share (EPS) growth of 19 percent in 1997 and nine percent in 1998.
"Despite prospects of higher rates we believe that there may still be upside to our EPS estimates," it said.
Merrill Lynch said it was overweight banks, conglomerates, media and property developers and underweight property investors and utilities.

Its top recommendations over the next 12 months following recent price weakness are Cheung Kong, CITIC Pacific, Dao Heng Bank, First Pacific, New World Development, Sun Hung Kai Properties, Swire Pacific, TVB, Wharf and Wheelock.
